recentItems.title: Irish Champions Festival 2026 Highlights: Every Winner from a Dramatic Weekend | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Highlights of every race from the Irish Champions Festival at Leopardstown and the Curragh.

Hotazhell caused a 50/1 shock in the Royal Bahrain Irish Champion Stakes, holding on by a nose from Wimbledon Hawkeye for Jessica Harrington and Shane Foley, with 11/8 favourite Constitution River third. Blue Bolt made it three Group 1 wins in three countries in the Matron, Darkness Falls took the Golden Fleece, and Arabian Crown made all in the Kilternan at 11/1 for a James Doyle double alongside Quddwah in the Solonaway.

At the Curragh on Sunday, Ryan Moore rode three of the four Group 1s — Sun Goddess in the Moyglare, Scandinavia in the Irish St Leger and Thundering On in the Blandford — with Comanche Brave taking the Flying Five and Folsom Blues the Vincent O'Brien National Stakes for Joseph O'Brien.

recentItems.description: Aidan O’Brien won two Group 1s with Sun Goddess (Moyglare) and (Scandinavia) at the Irish Champions Festival, but sons Joseph (Folsom Blues) and Donnacha (Comanche Brave) grabbed the liners man a memorable day for tbe O’Brien family at the Irish Champions Festival Festival.

recentItems.title: Scandinavia leads Aidan O'Brien 1-2-3 in Irish St. Leger | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Scandinavia cemented his status as the king of the staying division with a hard-fought victory in the Comer Group International Irish St. Leger.

Winner of the St Leger at Doncaster on this weekend 12 months ago, the Justify colt had continued his progress by winning each of his previous four starts this season including the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot in June and his second Goodwood Cup the following month.

The four-year-old was a 4-11 shot to extend his overall winning sequence to eight in the Irish Flat season’s final Classic and while his stablemate Queenstown proved a tough nut to crack on the front end, Scandinavia eventually wore him down and was ultimately well on top as he passed the post two lengths to the good.

O’Brien, who enjoyed a one-two-three as Jan Brueghel made late gains to pick up the bronze medal, said of Scandinavia: “He’s a great horse. He just has an unbelievable amount of stamina. He’s a big, high cruiser and we were delighted to have Queenstown there today to keep going along.

recentItems.title: Thundering On Back To Brilliant Best In Blandford Stakes | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Thundering On returned to winning ways when benefitting from a confident hold up ride by Ryan Moore to land the Group 2 Moyglare ‘Jewels' Blandford Stakes at the Curragh.

The Frankel filly took the Betfred Oaks at Epsom in impressive fashion but the combination of fast ground and a drop back in trip proved her undoing here subsequently in the Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes.

Moore held up the 5/4 favourite towards rear before making gradual progress in the straight and swept to the front inside the final furlong.

She kept on well to beat Lilt by a length and a half with Red Letter a nose further back in third.

The victory completed a four-timer on the afternoon for Moore while trainer Joseph O'Brien was saddling a treble.

recentItems.title: Folsom Blues Oozes Class In Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Folsom Blues upstaged his better fancied stablemate Monogram to claim top honours in the Goffs Vincent O’Brien National Stakes.

Having made a big impression on his course and distance debut three weeks ago, Monogram was the 9-4 favourite to successfully step up to Group One level for Joseph O’Brien, with his father Aidan’s Futurity winner Giant Sequoia and Oliver Cole’s British raider Dr Rascal rated his two biggest dangers.

But Folsom Blues brought strong Group One form to the table himself, having filled the runner-up spot best of the rest behind the earlier Moyglare Stud Stakes heroine Sun Goddess in last month’s Phoenix Stakes, and went one better in some style at 11-2 under Joey Sheridan.

Always travelling powerfully, the Blue Point colt engaged overdrive in the last of six furlongs to score by six lengths, with the less experienced Monogram making late gains into second to give his trainer a one-two.

recentItems.title: Target Set On The Breeders Cup For Comanche Brave Following Flying Five Win | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Comanche Brave and Billy Loughnane swooped late to supplement their July Cup success with victory in the BAR 1 Betting Flying Five Stakes at the Curragh.

Dropping back to five furlongs on his first start since his Group One breakthrough at Newmarket nine weeks ago, Donnacha O’Brien’s sprinter was the 5-2 favourite to double his top-level tally.

Loughnane gave his mount plenty of time to find his feet off the frenetic early pace, but he could be spotted travelling ominously well in behind American Affair approaching the final furlong.

His supporters will have been anxious for a few moments as he waited for the gap to appear, but when it did Comanche Brave quickly sealed the deal, accelerating away to score by a length and a quarter from American Affair, with another British raider in Rumstar a close-up third.

recentItems.title: Sun Goddess Shines in the Moyglare Stud Stakes | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Sun Goddess further enhanced her huge reputation with a runaway victory in the Moyglare Stud Stakes at the Curragh.

Aidan O’Brien’s filly had won four of her six previous starts, a record which includes a Group One victory against the boys in last month’s Phoenix Stakes and a demolition job in a valuable sales race at York on her latest outing.

Despite some concerns about the overall form of the Ballydoyle team, the daughter of Sioux Nation was the 4-7 favourite to notch a second top-level success on her first attempt at seven furlongs.

And after travelling strongly into contention in the hands of Ryan Moore, she rocketed six and a half lengths clear of the runner-up Green Empress, prompting Paddy Power slash her odds to 3-1 favourite from 7-1 for next year’s 1000 Guineas.
